title: Build or buy the scheduler?
logline: Buying gets us live seven months sooner for a known cost; we recommend buy with an exit clause.
audience: The steering group, deciding this week.

music.prompt: Sober cinematic minimalism, sustained strings, sparse piano, no percussion

beats.vo: One decision this week: do we build the scheduler, or buy it?
Today, scheduling takes our coordinators eleven hours a week. Either option brings that to about two.
Building gives full control but takes nine months. Buying is live in eight weeks, with less flexibility.
On the criteria that matter, buying covers audit, single sign-on and support; building only wins on customisation.
We recommend buy, with a two-year exit clause, and revisit building once the process is stable.
